answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers one hollow batch on the harbor board, from a canyon route, key-bound. Each epoch it returns the batch to the depot; auditors scan serials against issues, and a missing, duplicate, or foreign serial burns the bond. First return costs 28, the k-th batch from one wallet 28+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,022 and 1,000 fakes cost 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked, rising quadratically. A rented-return ring fails: rented batches cannot return twice, and duplicate serials are rejected. An honest agent pays 28 once and recovers its bond on a clean return.
